walkthroughs.body_html:
Paper 2: Modern Texts and Poetry — a core area of GCSE English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 2: Modern Texts and Poetry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Paper 2: Modern Texts and Poetry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In what war was the Light Brigade?
options: Boer
Crimean
Napoleonic
WWI
An unreliable narrator is when the author makes mistakes.
Enjambment is when a poem uses no punctuation at all.
An unreliable narrator is one who tells lies in the story.
Their account is undermined within the text by ignorance, bias, self-deception or deceit, so the reader must read against what they say.

mcqs.q: Why does historical context matter when reading literature?
options: Texts emerge from and respond to specific historical conditions — context illuminates references, assumptions and arguments that might otherwise be invisible.
Context just means writing about what the author had for breakfast.
Context is required because all texts are about history.
An unreliable narrator is when the author makes mistakes.
Context is required because all texts are about history.
Enjambment is when a poem has very long lines.
When a sentence or phrase runs over from one line of poetry to the next without a punctuated pause, creating flow or surprise across the line break.
Enjambment is when a poem uses no punctuation at all.
